answer: Sybil attackers arrive on a gale: thousands of light, cheap identities drifting like a zephyr through the inlet of an open agent economy. Stop them by making each agent lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it may trade, slashed for double-signing or spam, and by adding a slow-release ridge of reputation earned only through attested useful work over time, gating access to high-value jobs. A thousand sybils then costs a thousand stakes plus weeks of honest work each, while one honest agent passes with a single stake. The attack turns uneconomic before it turns effective.
